newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips close mixed, SAX down 4.42 pts.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips close mixed, SAX down 4.42 pts.

text.p: Major Slovak shares closed mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, with losses to several heavy-weighted issues pulling the SAX index down 4.42 points to 176.67.
Oil refiner Slovnaft, the most heavily-capitalised issue on the BSE floor, lost 23 crowns to close at 810, with an average price - used for calculating the index - down by 8.53 percent.

Brokers said that while Slovnaft traded within the range from 750 to 892 crowns, they saw its real price at around 800 crowns, a level at which larger packages were available on the market at the moment.
But they said that a relatively small amount of Slovnaft shares traded, only 9,035, made it hard to predict a further trend.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta closed up 210 crowns at 1,680, but its average price eased by 8.6 percent which, brokers said, also contributed to the SAX's decline.

Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said moves in Nafta's price were due mainly to traditional year-end accounting moves and that they did not reflect the real situation with the issue, which is still plagued by liquidity problems resulting from general uncertanity among investors over company's future.
Steel producer VSZ was the only real gainer among the blue chips, closing up 25 crowns at 625, with average price up one percent.

Overall volume decreased to 760,144 shares, with direct trades accounting for major part of deals, from 1,347,802 stocks traded on Friday. Turnover fell to 364.87 million crowns, from 1.11 billion crowns on Friday.
